name: Average cross-sectional correlation of daily returns as a risk state: basket exposure with hysteresis and minimum duration
mechanism: Exposure of the equal-weighted basket of listed pairs (1/n_eligible each, the rest in USDT) set by the average cross-sectional correlation. Each day, over the last L days, we compute the daily log returns of each pair listed over the whole window (a pair that is not listed or has an invalid day is dropped), then the average of the Pearson correlations between all retained pairs, rho (between -1 and 1, unitless, invariant to rescaling). At least 8 retained pairs are required, otherwise the previous state is kept (full basket at the start). Rule: full basket when rho >= c; back to USDT when rho < 0.6 x c; in between, previous state (fixed multiplicative hysteresis); minimum duration of each state: 10 days. Economic meaning (Pollet and Wilson): a high average correlation signals that common risk dominates the pairs' own risk, hence that non-diversifiable risk is high, and it predicts higher future excess returns of the aggregate market (risk premium as compensation); a low correlation, with strong cross-sectional dispersion, signals a market where information is pair-specific and the aggregate premium is low. The basket is held only when the aggregate risk premium is rewarded. Alternative hypothesis, equally testable: in crypto, correlation rises mostly in declines (everything is sold); if the effect exists in the opposite direction (high correlation followed by lower returns), the sheet is refuted by its sign. Difference from V1: we do not use the volatility level but the common share of the covariance; difference from A: no price spike, no past-return information. Fixed settings chosen a priori: exit ratio 0.6 and minimum holding of 10 days (turnover at most 7 full round trips per year), at least 8 pairs.

name: Market breadth (share of pairs above their own average): basket exposure with hysteresis and minimum holding duration
mechanism: The strategy does not pick pairs: it sets the exposure of the equal-weighted basket of listed pairs (weight 1/n_eligible each, the rest in USDT) according to an aggregate state, the breadth. Each day, for each pair listed for at least L days, we test whether its close is above its own simple average of the last L daily closes. The breadth B is the share of testable pairs that pass the test (between 0 and 1, unitless, hence invariant to rescaling of prices and volumes). Rule: full basket when B >= s; back to USDT when B < 0.6 x s; in between, we keep the previous state (multiplicative hysteresis fixed a priori). Minimum holding duration of each state: 10 days (the counter is kept by the strategy from the rank of the days in the stream). If fewer than 6 pairs are testable, the previous state is kept (full basket at the very beginning). Mechanism: a rise carried by a minority of pairs (low breadth) is fragile; it reflects capital concentrated in a few names (narratives, leverage on a few assets) and demand that has not spread. A broad rise reflects a diffuse capital inflow, more durable, and a broad decline reflects a general disengagement whose adjustment is slow (chained forced sales from one asset to another, liquidity withdrawing from the whole segment). Breadth is a market state, not a past return of each pair: the signal is a cross-sectional aggregate and the execution is an exposure setting, not a selection. Difference from T1 (per-pair trend, per-pair decision): here the decision is single for the whole basket and depends on the cross-sectional consensus; difference from B (k best pairs): no pair is favored; difference from V1: the signal is not volatility. A priori choice of the fixed settings: exit ratio 0.6 (wide band, to limit turnover), minimum holding of 10 days (at most two switches per month), equal weights on all listed pairs when invested (and not on those above their average) so that turnover comes only from state switches. The maximum annual turnover of 15 corresponds to at most 7 full round trips per year: the band and the minimum duration hold it across the whole grid, including at the most nervous setting (L = 20, lowest s).

name: Delayed catch-up of follower pairs on the factor of central pairs, with hysteresis and minimum duration
mechanism: Slow information diffusion hypothesis: large pairs, more liquid and more closely followed, incorporate news common to the whole market before small ones, which respond with a delay (Hou 2007: the lag of small firms behind large ones is a slow-diffusion effect). Columns are anonymous and volumes are rebased per pair, so the strategy cannot know "the large pair"; it infers it from returns. Every 30 days (internal counter of the stream, no date), the m = 3 most central pairs are designated leaders: those whose average correlation with the other pairs, over the last 90 daily returns, is highest (90 valid days are required). R_m(d) is the average of their daily log returns. For each other pair j we estimate over 90 days the slope beta_j of r_j on R_m (contemporaneous, bounded to [0; 3]) and the standard deviation sigma_j of the residual r_j - beta_j R_m. Over the last h days, the catch-up gap is G_j = (beta_j * sum(R_m) - sum(r_j)) / (sigma_j * sqrt(h)): how much less the pair followed the leaders than its beta predicts, in standard deviations of its own noise. Entry: G_j >= theta AND sum(R_m) > 0 (the lag is a lag only if the leaders moved up; otherwise the signal would be a simple idiosyncratic mean reversion, which the lab covers with A). Exit: G_j <= 0.25 theta (catch-up done, clear hysteresis) or 28 days of holding, never before 5 days (minimum duration). Weight 1/n_eligible per pair held, the rest in USDT. The 1h aggregates are only used to compute daily returns (close to close of the 00:00 bar); the decision takes place once a day. Fixed settings (fixed_params) chosen a priori: estimation window 90 days (long enough for a stable beta, short enough to follow changes in market structure), 3 leaders (less noisy average than 1, without diluting toward the whole market), exit at 25% of the threshold (wide band that limits turnover), holding 5 to 28 days. The leaders themselves are not held on this signal (their gap is zero by construction). Difference from the existing families: A is an absolute rebound after a decline, B/T1 are the pair's own momentum, F1 uses the taker flow; here the signal is a gap conditional on a common factor measured on the other pairs.
